target_customer: Pharma and biotech developers of protein and phage-based drugs; clinical programs for personalized phage therapy
problem: Producing novel biological drugs, especially synthetic bacteriophages for antibiotic-resistant infections, is slow and costly with cell-based methods.
business_model: Platform biotech (cell-free protein synthesis, Phactory) aiming at phage therapeutics and partnered drug production; pre-revenue grants-funded
product_category: Cell-free synthetic biology for protein and phage drugs

founders.name: Patrick Grossmann
education: Harvard Medical School and ETH Zurich (bioinformatics training)

founders.name: Kilian Vogele
founders.background_notes: Holds five patents per the YC page; role labels differ across articles.

competitors.name: Adaptive Phage Therapeutics
competitors.what: Clinical-stage phage therapy company (PhageBank, prosthetic joint infection trials)
competitors.traction_then: Received US DoD funding for clinical advancement of phage (Sept 2021)

technical_complexity.rationale: Cell-free assembly of functional phages and proteins from DNA was a research result (Cell Chemical Biology paper) and still needs GMP-grade, clinically validated production.

defensibility.rationale: Patent-pending platform and university IP, but unproven at clinical scale; amount of freedom to operate unknown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquisition or copying found through 2026.

market_need_then: Antimicrobial resistance is a recognized public-health crisis; EU and non-dilutive funders (INCATE, EIC) backed the effort in 2022 to 2025.

identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific; tagline Breaking Biology Free appears on a directory listing.

branding.brand_signature: Phactory platform name (from the 2018 TUM iGEM team)

brand_strength.rationale: Name resembles the term in vitro but no source states the origin; no evidence of brand-driven awareness in a B2B biotech setting.

outcome_analysis: Invitris is an early-stage TUM spin-out from the 2018 iGEM Phactory team whose public funding is grants (INCATE 2022 and 2023, EIC Accelerator selection 2025) rather than disclosed venture rounds. It has not exited or shut down; the main risks are clinical translation and raising equity for GMP production, which remain unresolved as of 2026.
notes: INCATE Stage II amount was EUR 250,000 (June 2023); Stage I approved January 2022 with amount not stated; amounts left null rather than converting currency. EIC Accelerator amount not stated (described only as multi-million). Aggregator totals ($1.0M, $3.5M, $500K pre-seed) conflict and are unverified. Founding date: YC says 2022 (GmbH registration) while the team originated in the 2018 iGEM project. Competitor list holds one entry dated after the batch window start; no earlier dated sources for cell-free phage rivals found.
